html:
Hainan is a large tropical island off the south coast of China, across a narrow strait from the mainland. The map shows it from 1 CE to 1400 as a frontier of Chinese empires, often only loosely held.

Its first people are the Hlai, or Li, who speak a language of the Kra Dai family. After the Han conquest of Nanyue in 111 BCE, the Han dynasty set up two commanderies on the island. Revolts were constant, and in 46 BCE the court gave up the main one.

Under the Tang and Song dynasties, Chinese counties grew along the coasts while the Hlai held the mountains. The island became a place of exile for officials who lost favour. The poet Su Shi spent three years there at the end of his life, from 1097 to 1100. Ships on the sea routes to Southeast Asia stopped at its ports.

Hlai women were skilled at spinning and weaving cotton. In the late 1200s, under the Yuan, the weaver Huang Daopo is said to have learned their methods on Hainan and taken them home to Songjiang, near Shanghai, which became a great cotton cloth centre. Under the Ming the island was firmly part of Guangdong province. It became a province of its own in 1988.
sum: Hainan is a large tropical island off the south coast of China, across a narrow strait from the mainland. The map shows it from 1 CE to 1400 as a frontier of Chinese empires, often only loosely held.
